question: Does any low-variance composition rule over the two certified v7 parents beat the deployed 50/50 logit mean on net pairs, fold by fold?

why_new.measured_motivation: phase19 shared-error atlas: 14.9% of the champion's failing pairs are aggregation losses (one parent orders the pair correctly); pooled aggregation_loss_auc_mass = 0.005599748393447816. Composition has therefore more recoverable mass than any single stored model can supply (best stored blend gain <= +1.5e-5 at w=0.10 over ~1600 scanned comparisons, i.e. at the noise level).
prior_attempts: equal / softmax / family-balanced global weights: <= champion (phase 20/21)
covariate gating ENS72: +1.01e-5 over equal blend, gate could not generalise
nested stacks with 285 features: no admission
why_new.material_difference: Every prior corrector had hundreds of inputs and therefore hundreds of effective degrees of freedom against ~4.8e9 pairs per fold but only 5 fold-level units of evidence. This lab restricts the combiner to (i) zero-parameter nonlinearities of the two parent scores, or (ii) at most 5 fitted parameters, all fitted on FIT rows only. It is a variance-reduction hypothesis, not a capacity hypothesis.

test_side.note: test-side parents are the certified full-data-context route and the full-data-refit aux10; recomposition costs 0 model fits

rules.C1_nested_weight: per fold k, w_k on a fixed grid 0.30..0.70 step 0.025 maximising AUC on the FIT rows of fold k (FIT rows scored by their own outer-OOF values); apply w_k to the eval fold
rules.C2_block_rank: within the evaluated block, u_p = (rank(p)-0.5)/n for each parent; score = u_r + u_a (0 fitted parameters)
rules.C3_fit_cdf: per fold k, map each parent through the empirical CDF of the FIT rows of fold k; score = u_r + u_a
rules.C4_confidence_logistic: logistic regression (L2=1.0, lbfgs, max_iter=1000) on [z_r, z_a, |z_r-z_a|, min(z_r,z_a), max(z_r,z_a)] fitted on FIT rows of fold k
rules.C5_platt_average: two independent Platt scalings (logistic on z_p alone, FIT rows only), then average the calibrated logits

confirmation_sensitivity.fitting_for_two_fold_arms: leave-one-shadow-fold-out: parameters for fold f are fitted on the rows of the other shadow fold only
confirmation_sensitivity.role: sensitivity only: different fitted models and different partitions, but only 279,854 rows and the same underlying data

statistics: mean paired per-fold delta vs C0 and its paired fold SE (sd/sqrt(5))
Holm adjustment over the 7 non-control rules

promotion_gate.shadow_sensitivity: mean delta > 0 and both shadow folds > 0 (sensitivity, not independent proof)
promotion_gate.action_on_pass: freeze the rule, build the test composition from the certified parents, certify, and only then open a separate SUBMISSION_DECISION under PATH A; zero submissions before that
promotion_gate.action_on_fail: record NO_ADMISSION in the ledger; the two-parent composition geometry is then closed as a measured negative and v7 stays unchanged

failure_conditions: any rule reaching the gate through a rule fitted on eval-fold labels (would be leakage; the implementation asserts FIT/eval disjointness)
C0 identity replication error > 1e-6 against the certified portfolio
test-side recomposition error > 1e-6 against the certified candidate SHA
multiple_testing_disclosure: 7 rules are tested in one frozen family. Holm covers these 7. It does not cover the ~600 historical experiments, nor the fact that the primary folds have already been used for selection many times. A pass is therefore evidence for a small effect, not proof.

leakage_analysis.C3: CDF from FIT rows only; no labels
leakage_analysis.C1_C4_C5: labels used, FIT rows only, never the eval fold; FIT rows are scored by outer-OOF values produced by models that never saw them
leakage_analysis.known_limitation: stacking features for FIT rows come from other fold models than for eval rows (standard stacking distribution mismatch, unchanged from the project's earlier nested stacks)
